source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Body Fluids and Circulation
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: A person of blood group AB is called a universal recipient because the plasma lacks
questions.explanation: AB red cells carry both A and B antigens, so the plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B.

questions.stem: In a normal ECG, the P wave is produced by
questions.explanation: P records spread of the impulse over the atria; QRS is ventricular depolarisation; T is ventricular recovery.

questions.stem: The sino-atrial node that starts each heartbeat lies in the wall of the
questions.explanation: SAN is in the upper right atrium near the opening of the superior vena cava.

questions.stem: The most abundant plasma protein, which also maintains colloid osmotic pressure, is
questions.explanation: Albumin is the chief plasma protein; globulins include antibodies; fibrinogen is for clotting.

questions.stem: The average life span of a circulating human erythrocyte is about
questions.explanation: Mature RBCs live roughly 120 days and are then removed mainly by the spleen.

questions.stem: Thrombin formed during clotting converts fibrinogen into insoluble
questions.explanation: Thrombin polymerises fibrinogen to fibrin threads that trap cells and seal the wound.

questions.stem: Blood from the intestine reaches the liver before the heart through the
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries absorbed nutrients to the liver for processing.

questions.stem: The first heart sound (lub) is produced by the closure of the
questions.explanation: Lub marks the start of ventricular systole when mitral and tricuspid valves shut.

questions.stem: Cardiac output is defined as the product of heart rate and
questions.explanation: CO = SV × HR; about 70 mL × 72/min gives roughly 5 litres per minute at rest.

questions.stem: Chest pain on exertion due to incomplete oxygen supply to the heart wall is called
questions.explanation: Angina is myocardial ischaemia, usually from narrowed coronary arteries.

questions.stem: Erythroblastosis foetalis may occur when the mother is Rh-negative and the foetus is
questions.explanation: Anti-Rh antibodies from a sensitised Rh- mother can destroy Rh+ foetal RBCs.

questions.stem: The QRS complex of the ECG corresponds to
questions.explanation: QRS is the electrical event that triggers ventricular contraction; atrial recovery is hidden in it.

questions.stem: A complete cardiac cycle lasts about 0.8 s at 72 beats/min. Of this, ventricular systole occupies roughly 0.3 s. The remaining 0.5 s is mainly
options: joint diastole plus atrial systole (ventricular filling)
the time taken for blood to reach the feet
questions.explanation: After ejection, both chambers relax (joint diastole) and atria then contract to finish ventricular filling.

questions.stem: Red cells of blood group O can be given to A, B or AB recipients because they lack
options: both anti-A and anti-B in the plasma only
questions.explanation: Group O erythrocytes have no A/B antigens, so recipient antibodies do not agglutinate them.

questions.stem: The T wave of a standard ECG represents
questions.explanation: T is recovery of ventricular muscle; atrial repolarisation is masked by the QRS.

questions.stem: The correct sequence of the cardiac conducting system is
options: AV node → SAN → Purkinje → bundle of His
SAN → AV node → bundle of His → Purkinje fibres
Purkinje → SAN → AV node → bundle of His
Bundle of His → SAN → AV node → Purkinje
questions.explanation: The impulse starts at SAN, delays at AVN, then races through the bundle and Purkinje network.

questions.stem: Which plasma protein is chiefly concerned with defence (antibodies)?
questions.explanation: Gamma globulins are immunoglobulins; albumin is osmotic; fibrinogen is clotting.

questions.stem: Which formed element is a cell fragment that helps in clotting?
questions.explanation: Platelets are megakaryocyte fragments; they release clotting factors at injury sites.

questions.stem: Calcium ions and vitamin K are required in clotting because they help form
questions.explanation: Several clotting factors (including prothrombin conversion) need Ca2+; vitamin K is needed to make some of those factors.

questions.stem: Lymph differs from blood plasma mainly in having
options: much less protein and no RBCs
questions.explanation: Lymph is filtered plasma with fewer proteins and no red cells; it does carry lymphocytes.

questions.stem: The valve that prevents backflow from the aorta into the left ventricle is the
questions.explanation: Aortic semilunar cusps close at the start of ventricular diastole, producing the second heart sound.

questions.stem: In human double circulation, the pulmonary circuit starts from the
questions.explanation: Deoxygenated blood is pumped by the right ventricle through pulmonary arteries to the lungs.

questions.stem: A resting blood pressure that stays above 140/90 mm Hg is termed
questions.explanation: Sustained high arterial pressure is hypertension and strains heart and vessels.

questions.stem: A person of group A can safely receive packed red cells from which donor group besides A?
questions.explanation: Group A plasma has anti-B, so B or AB cells would agglutinate; O cells lack A and B antigens.

questions.stem: Which ECG event is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation: The P wave is atrial, not ventricular; ventricular systole follows the QRS.

questions.stem: During the brief AV nodal delay, blood continues to flow from atria into ventricles. This delay is useful because it
options: allows atrial systole to finish ventricular filling before ventricular contraction
closes the semilunar valves at the start of atrial systole
questions.explanation: The 0.1 s pause at the AV node lets atria empty; then the ventricles contract on a full load.
